cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: What Are We Now?
cards.instruction: Find out how someone defines the relationship without directly asking for a label.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Do I bring my own towel when I visit now?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. The guest towel or the one that's always been mine?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yours is still on the hook. I haven't moved it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When I leave, shall I hang it back there or put it with the guest laundry?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 asks what to bring and A5 asks where to leave it; the status prefixes do not alter the deferential guest tactic despite clear D78 probing.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 use one here prompts A3 guest/personal distinction; B4 unchanged hook prompts A5 future placement test.

relationship.evidence: B2 offers hospitality and B4 reports not moving the towel, giving plausible ambiguous information.

heightening.evidence: B4 unchanged object could be inertia, so A5 asks an active future choice rather than assuming continued belonging.

specificity.evidence: A1 visiting now and A3 formerly personal towel establish changed uncertainty without needing a breakup story.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 guest laundry versus personal hook is earned; stock commands add tonal noise.
